The customer dimension is an SCD2 table. 30 customers have two rows: a historical row (is_current = False, valid_from 2023-06-01) and a current row (is_current = True, valid_from 2025-01-01). Joining on customer_id alone duplicates those customers' transactions, which explains 5251 vs 4558 (693 extra rows).

The fix is to build silver_customers from current rows only. All 200 customers have exactly one current row, so the join becomes 1:1. Every transaction in the window falls after 2025-01-01, so the current row is also the one valid at transaction time. Filtering on is_current keeps the columns and meaning of silver_customers unchanged.

gold_customer_spend and the other tables do not use the customer join, so they are unaffected.

I considered whether region should be as-of the transaction date. valid_from of the current row is 2025-01-01, before all transactions, and the historical rows are older, so the current row is correct for every transaction.
